summary:
Illes Balears stands under the national framework of Spain: Ley 4/2023 of 28 February 2023 on real and effective equality for trans persons and the guarantee of LGBTI rights applies uniformly across Spain's autonomous communities, and no deviation by this autonomous community from the national position is material enough to be scored separately (within ±0.02).

Under Article 43 of that law, any person aged 16 or over may request rectification of the gender mention on their own registry entry directly before the Civil Registry. Adults may therefore rectify the registered sex entry without prior surgical reassignment, and the right to the registered change is grounded in the free development of personality under Article 10.1 of the Spanish Constitution. This administrative route replaces the former requirement of a gender-dysphoria diagnosis plus two years of medical treatment; Human Rights Watch described the resulting regime as legal gender recognition by self-identification through a simple administrative process.

Recognition is possible from age 12 under conditions, and the law regulates consent for medical procedures on minors aged 12 to 16. Human Rights Watch records that the provision for children proved contentious during the law's passage.

Access to sex-separated facilities rests on legal gender self-determination rather than on biological sex, so the gender marker recorded in the civil registry is the operative basis for facility rules in Illes Balears as elsewhere in Spain.

Transphobic motivation operates as an aggravating circumstance in sentencing under Article 22.4 of the Criminal Code, and the hate-speech provision at Article 510 carries one to four years' imprisonment plus a fine of six to twelve months. Gender expression appears in no article of the Criminal Code, so a gender-expression-based hate crime has no free-standing offence.

Courts are applying the aggravation in practice. In Vigo, a Tribunal de Instancia used the transfobia aggravation for the first time in a misdemeanour case over WhatsApp messages threatening a trans woman and fined the author EUR 300. In Valencia, a juvenile gang that harassed, insulted, beat and filmed a trans person in a park to mock them produced a six-month prison sentence for the only adult defendant, while two minors were judged separately.
tangentialFactors:
With administrative self-declaration, Spain stands alongside Argentina, Ireland, Portugal and Uruguay in comparative treatment of legal gender recognition, and Spain is recognised in comparative rankings as among the most LGBT-friendly countries.

Both the sentencing aggravation and the hate-speech offence derive from Organic Law 6/2022 rather than from Ley 4/2023. Ley 4/2023 did reform the offences against sexual freedom at Articles 132, 173, 178 to 181 and 189 bis of the Criminal Code.

Human Rights Watch (16 February 2023) reports that the Spanish Congress's passage of the national Trans Law strengthened protections for unmarried same-sex couples. Same-sex marriage and full adoption rights have applied in Spain since 2005.
localsOnly:
Ley 4/2023 defines and sanctions discriminatory conduct and harassment on grounds of sexual orientation, sexual identity, gender expression and sexual characteristics, and declares discriminatory contract clauses null and void. It obliges collection of discrimination data broken down by the causes covered and mandates measures adapted to rural circumstances.

Residents of Illes Balears use the same Civil Registry route described above; the law also regulates consent for medical procedures on minors aged 12 to 16 and permits recognition from age 12 under conditions.

The national law combats LGBTI discrimination in healthcare, employment and housing, and strengthens protections for unmarried same-sex couples.
outOfScopeNotes:
No enforcement data specific to Illes Balears is sourced. The two judicial examples of the transphobia aggravation in operation, in Vigo and in Valencia, come from other provinces of Spain and are cited as illustration of national practice.

Entry, visa and border-screening rules that could expose a trans visitor's documents at arrival are not sourced in the inventory for Spain or for this autonomous community.

Whether the Govern de les Illes Balears has issued its own implementing regulations, budgets or guidance under Ley 4/2023 is unresolved in the inventory; the claim of no material regional deviation rests on a scoring assessment rather than on a sourced regional instrument.

Practice on facility access, including any dispute over multi-occupancy versus single-stall spaces, is not sourced beyond the rule that the civil-registry gender marker is operative.
